away.name: Mackenzie Blackwood
away.news: Since the start of the 2026-27 season, Head Coach Jared Bednar has leaned on Mackenzie Blackwood over Scott Wedgewood, who has struggled to start the campaign. That said, Wedgewood's struggles aside, Blackwood has earned his increased workload. The 29-year-old Blackwood was excellent in his most recent outing, recording his first shutout of the season, with a 27-save performance in a 4-0 win over the Detroit Red Wings. Colorado enters Tuesday's game as -160 road favourites against a struggling Toronto Maple Leafs team that has been outscored 11-4 during a three-game losing streak (0-3-0).

home.name: Sergei Bobrovsky
home.news: When the Maple Leafs signed Bobrovsky to a three-year, $7 million AAV contract ($21M total) in the offseason, the hope was that he could solidify their crease and return the team to the postseason. That said, Bobrovsky has struggled to start his tenure with the Maple Leafs, posting a subpar 3.34 GAA and .886 SV% in 12 games (3-7-2). Even more alarming, Bobrovsky has allowed three or more goals in all but one of his 12 outings. The veteran 38-year-old goalie hopes to snap a four-game losing streak on Tuesday, as the Maple Leafs enter as +146 home underdogs against a Colorado Avalanche team coming off a 4-0 win over the Detroit Red Wings.

away.name: Jesper Wallstedt
away.news: Wallstedt has been busy with Filip Gustavsson (hip) sidelined and will return to the crease for the 17th time in Minnesota's first 20 games. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie has been outstanding to start the 2026-27 season, giving Head Coach John Hynes no reason to deviate, posting a stellar 1.99 GAA and .922 SV% in 16 games (11-2-3). He has allowed two or fewer goals in six of his last seven games (5-1-1). The Wild enter Tuesday's contest as -121 road favourites against a Montreal Canadiens team with points in 10 straight games (8-0-2).

home.name: Jacob Fowler
home.news: Fowler was outstanding in the opening month of the season, posting a 1.84 GAA and .932 SV% in eight October games (7-1-0). That said, he had a catastrophic meltdown in his first game of November, as the Montreal Canadiens blew a 4-0 lead over the Winnipeg Jets in the final three minutes of an eventual 5-4 overtime loss. That said, the 21-year-old Fowler wasn't phased by the loss, bouncing back in his most recent game with a solid outing, saving 26 of 28 shots (.929 SV%) in a 4-2 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs. The Canadiens enter Tuesday's game as +110 home underdogs against the Central Division-leading Minnesota Wild.

away.name: Logan Thompson
away.news: Thompson has quietly become one of the NHL's most consistent and reliable goalies over the past several seasons, coming off consecutive 31-win campaigns. That said, the 29-year-old goalie has been inconsistent at the start of the 2026-27 season. Thompson was serviceable in his most recent outing, saving 27 of 30 shots (.900 SV%) in a 4-3 win over the Florida Panthers, but it marked the sixth time in his last eight games (3-5-0) that he has allowed three or more goals. The Capitals enter Tuesday's game with even -105 odds on the road against an Ottawa Senators team that is 3-1-0 in their last four games.

home.name: Samuel Ersson
home.news: Linus Ullmark (lower body) has ramped up intensity at practice, but will remain sidelined for at least one more game, with Ersson tending the twine on Tuesday. The 27-year-old Ersson had a rough start to his tenure with the Senators but has played well in recent games, prompting the team to take extra precautions with Ullmark's return. Ersson is riding a three-game winning streak, in which he has saved 76 of 80 shots (.950 SV%). The Senators enter Tuesday's game with even -105 odds at home against the Washington Capitals, who are coming off a 4-3 win over the Florida Panthers.

away.name: Jacob Markstrom
away.news: Markstrom has struggled since returning from a multi-week absence due to an upper-body injury, allowing three or more goals in three games (1-2-0), posting an .871 SV%. The 36-year-old Swedish goalie's return to Florida has been inconsistent, posting a pedestrian 2.74 GAA and an .886 SV% in nine appearances (4-3-1). Still, the Panthers enter Tuesday's game as -112 road favourites against a Columbus Blue Jackets team they defeated 7-3 less than a month ago.

home.name: Cam Talbot
home.news: Jet Greaves was expected to lead the way between the pipes for Columbus this season, but early-season struggles have awarded Talbot increased playing time. That said, Greaves' struggles aside, Talbot has played well lately and earned his share of starts. The veteran 39-year-old goalie was excellent in his most recent outing, saving 31 of 32 shots (.969 SV%) in a 2-1 shootout win over the Dallas Stars. He has an outstanding 1.69 GAA and .942 SV% in his last four games (4-0-0). The Blue Jackets enter Tuesday's game as +104 home underdogs against a Florida Panthers team that is 1-3-0 in their last four games.

away.name: John Gibson
away.news: Gibson has missed a week with a lower-body injury, but he will return to the crease on Tuesday. The 33-year-old Gibson nearly single-handedly led the Red Wings to the playoffs last season before falling just short, but he has struggled to start the 2026-27 campaign. Gibson has an ugly 3.46 GAA and .860 SV% in 11 appearances this season (4-5-1), and has allowed three or more goals six times. The Red Wings enter Tuesday's contest as +124 road underdogs against a Blues team that defeated them 5-4 less than two weeks ago.

home.name: Joel Hofer
home.news: Hofer has been reliable on most nights, earning his share of the crease and making veteran Jordan Binnington the clear-cut backup goalie in St. Louis. The 26-year-old Hofer is coming off a solid outing, saving 26 of 28 shots (.929 SV%), but lost 3-1 to the Nashville Predators. Goal support has been a recurring issue for Hofer lately, as the Blues have only scored four goals combined in his last three losses, despite him saving 142 of 155 shots (.916 SV%). The Blues enter Tuesday's game as -138 home favourites against a Detroit Red Wings team that has only scored three goals combined in their last three games (0-3-0).

away.name: Jake Allen
away.news: In a highly anticipated game, the Devils management has opted to bench Connor Hellebuyck against his former team on Tuesday. Instead, the Devils will turn to Jake Allen, who has struggled against the Winnipeg Jets in his career, posting a 3.18 GAA and .884 SV% in 24 appearances (9-11-3). The 36-year-old goalie has allowed four or more goals in four of his last six games (4-2-0), posting a 3.45 GAA and .874 SV%.

home.name: Nico Daws
home.news: Daws hasn't seen much action since being acquired by the Winnipeg Jets in a trade nearly three weeks ago, starting just a single game where he allowed four goals on 37 shots (.892 SV%) in a 5-2 loss to the Florida Panthers. Winnipeg's crease remains uncertain, and if Daws can string together some solid outings, he can earn himself an increased workload. The Jets enter Tuesday's contest as +132 home underdogs against Daws' former team, the New Jersey Devils, who are riding a five-game winning streak.

home.name: Anton Forsberg
home.news: Darcy Kuemper struggled last season, leading the Kings to rely on Forsberg toward the end of the season and into the playoffs, creating uncertainty heading into 2026-27. That said, the Kings have relied on Kuemper to start the season, despite Forsberg's solid play. The 33-year-old Forsberg has yet to win in six appearances (0-4-1), but has been solid, allowing two or fewer goals four times. He has a 2.51 GAA and a .902 SV%. The Kings enter Tuesday's game as -125 home favourites against the Nashville Predators, who are riding a four-game winning streak.
